money.note: Individuals gave $14,262,069; PAC money $1,000; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Attorney and Democratic U.S. representative for California's 17th District since 2017. Earlier he was a deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Commerce (2009–2011), a Silicon Valley law firm attorney, and a Stanford lecturer.

controversies.text: Missed 11 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.6%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 2, 2025-05-13 to 2025-05-13.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, End Citizens United, Equality California and California Environmental Voters.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements by Khanna on data centers or on slowing development. We found no record of his position on eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, Second Amendment issues, or school vouchers and charters. We also couldn't establish what year he moved to California. His Ballotpedia profile says he did not complete its candidate survey in any recent cycle. The Wikipedia page was cut off before its sections on his remaining policy positions and later career, so those were not reviewed.

cands.name: Ritesh Tandon

money.note: Individuals gave $56,986; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $25. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Engineer and business executive in Silicon Valley. He was CEO of Kricel Corporation, worked at Cisco for 11 years, and was a research fellow at UC Berkeley. He has a Santa Clara University master's degree and MBA. He has run for Congress in CA-17 several times and has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter-guide recommendations in 2026 from Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide and the San Francisco and California urbanism Sway guide.
In his April 2026 survey he says he is endorsed by the California Congress of Republicans and the Silicon Valley Chinese Association (candidate's own claim).

cands.gaps: His birthplace and where he was raised are not stated on the pages reviewed; he was educated in India and came to the U.S. at 28. He has held no elected office, so there is no record of official actions. We found no independent reporting confirming his claimed role in Tandon v. Newsom or his claims about the Prop 16, SB 403 and recall campaigns. We found no stated positions from him on guns, abortion, or limits on investor or foreign land buying. We found no news coverage of controversies. The campaign homepage text was cut off partway through the 'About' section.

qual.background: Engineer and tech executive: 11 years at Cisco, then 24 years in tech before founding his own company (CEO of Kricel Corporation), plus a UC Berkeley research fellowship. He has held no elected or governing office.
qual.why: Business and executive management experience fits the middle band. He has no legislative, legal or budget-office record, and his five runs for Congress are not offices held.
qual.label: Business and executive management experience fits the middle band. He has no legislative, legal or budget-office record, and his five runs for Congress are not offices held.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Campaign platform calls for firm timelines for federal approvals of data centers, semiconductor facilities and similar projects, and says 'Fast-track permits for data centers, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing.'

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Campaign site states a long-term tax reform goal of lowering state income taxes toward 5% and property taxes toward 0.25%, phased in and tied to spending reductions.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he will fight to build more homes by cutting the red tape and delays that drive up construction costs, and backs federal incentives for new housing supply and faster local permitting.

workers-first.evidence: Immigration platform calls for border security, stronger employer verification, ending 'catch-and-release,' accelerated removal of those who threaten community safety, and H-1B reform with stricter employer accountability, wage floors and anti-abuse audits. It also supports expanding merit-based pathways for high-skill talent.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says 'Fund the child, not the bureaucracy — public, charter, or parents' choice' (April 2026 survey). His 2024 website called for making school choice a mandatory law with tax dollars following the student.

back-police-order.evidence: Pledges to back police and first responders with the resources they need while insisting on accountability and fairness, and to push federal support against retail theft and fentanyl trafficking.
